title: Make
summary: A visual automation platform built around scenarios, module actions and monthly credits.

sources.title: Make Core pricing and annual billing

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: Visual scenarios connect applications through triggers and actions that process data.

facts.label: Usage unit
facts.value: The pricing page describes module actions as credits and exposes selectable monthly credit quantities.

prices.name: Free
prices.billing: Free plan; official page says there is no time limit.

prices.name: Core (10,000 credits/month; annual billing)
prices.billing: Make lists USD 9/month equivalent for 10,000 monthly credits on annual billing; this is not the upfront annual total or regional checkout quote.
prices.allowance: 10,000 credits per month at the selected pricing quantity.

prices.name: Core (10,000 credits/month; monthly billing)
prices.billing: The Make pricing selector lists USD 12/month at the 10,000-credit tier with monthly payment; local taxes and checkout total depend on location.
prices.allowance: 10,000 credits per month at the selected pricing quantity.
prices.taxes: Location-dependent checkout taxes are not captured.

sections.heading: Count actions, not just scenarios
paragraphs: List each trigger and module action in a representative scenario and estimate its run frequency. Retries, polling and data transfer can change the monthly credit requirement, so validate the estimate against a bounded trial.

sections.heading: Verify the billing selector
paragraphs: For 10,000 monthly credits, Make lists USD 12/month with monthly payment or USD 9/month equivalent on annual billing. Confirm location-dependent taxes, checkout details and extra-credit rules before budgeting.

pros.text: Make's visual scenario workflow connects applications through triggers and actions that process data.
The credit documentation distinguishes fixed and dynamic consumption, giving users a unit they can inspect during a trial.

cons.text: Credit use may be dynamic: AI and advanced features can vary with tokens, file size, page count or processing time.
A displayed monthly credit quantity alone does not establish the cost of a scenario; module behavior and billing cadence must be checked.

faqs.question: Does every Make action use exactly one credit?
faqs.answer: No. Most fixed-use app modules default to one credit per operation, while exceptions and dynamic AI or advanced features can consume a different amount.

faqs.question: What does Make Core cost for 10,000 monthly credits?
faqs.answer: The official pricing selector lists USD 12/month with monthly payment or USD 9/month equivalent on annual billing. Confirm location-dependent taxes and the final checkout total.

faqs.question: How should I estimate a scenario?
faqs.answer: Map its triggers, action modules, bundles and run frequency, then test retries and any AI, file or page processing against the current credit rules.

verdict: Evaluate Make when a visual scenario builder and a broad app-connection workflow fit the use case. Forecast module actions and verify the current pricing selectors before estimating cost.
bestFor: Builders who prefer visual automation and can map expected module actions
notFor: Teams that need a verified self-hosted deployment or a fixed cost without a usage estimate
migration: Export scenario definitions where supported, inventory connections and credentials separately, then replay representative events in a test organization before replacing the source workflow.
gaps: Confirm location-dependent checkout taxes and total, data retention, privacy, regional hosting and scenario export behavior for the intended plan.
A representative workflow has not been measured; credit use can vary by module and usage.
